planting.note: Set container divisions in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in bright shade to shade; this stoloniferous Chinese species resents soggy soil, so avoid low spots that collect winter moisture.

directions: Giant Chinese wild ginger forms slowly spreading clumps of large, glossy, evergreen leaves heavily mottled with silver, among the biggest foliage in the genus. Unusually large purple-and-yellow speckled flowers open at ground level in spring, hidden beneath the leaf canopy. Give it bright shade to full shade and even moisture in rich, well-drained soil; it is heat- and humidity-tolerant once established, making it a strong choice for warm-climate woodland gardens.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in light to full shade; this miniature selection spreads slowly, so keep it away from aggressive groundcover neighbors while it fills in.

directions: A Don Jacobs selection of the rare Southeastern native Asarum naniflorum, Eco Decor forms a miniature spreading mat of half-dollar-sized, shiny dark green leaves overlaid with dramatic silver veining, resembling a small-scale version of the popular 'Callaway' ginger. Small yellow flowers open in spring but stay hidden beneath the foliage. Plant in light to full shade in humus-rich soil; once established it tolerates drier shade better than many wild gingers.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to full shade; established plants tolerate drier shade conditions than most eastern wild gingers once their roots are settled.

directions: Selected along the Cahaba River in Alabama, this vigorous form of the southeastern native mottled wild ginger carries dark green, silver-patterned evergreen leaves over a compact, slowly spreading clump. Large, flared, dark purple flowers open in late spring but stay tucked just beneath the foliage. It tolerates dry shade better than many wild gingers, making it useful for difficult root-filled areas under established trees.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in rich, humus-laden, evenly moist, well-drained soil in light to full shade, sheltered from winter wind; this Chinese species responds strongly to fertile soil.

directions: Green Panda is a solid-green-leaved selection of the Chinese species Asarum maximum, grown chiefly for its remarkable two-inch flowers — velvet-black on the outside with a startling white interior, resembling a panda's face when viewed from above. Broad, glossy, evergreen leaves form an attractive clump; part the foliage in spring to find the ground-level blooms, since they are otherwise easily overlooked. Less cold-hardy than American or European wild gingers, it performs best in warm-temperate gardens with consistent moisture and winter shelter.

planting.note: Set divisions in spring into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in light to full shade; growth is extremely slow and low, so this selection suits small-scale plantings rather than fast groundcover use.

directions: Pitter Patter is a dwarf Japanese wild ginger with silver-dollar-sized, deep green evergreen leaves marked by a large central silver pattern, forming an unusually flat, low mat only an inch or two tall. Tiny purple flowers open in late winter hidden beneath the foliage. Its diminutive scale makes it well suited to rock gardens, troughs, or the front edge of a shaded bed, where it spreads gradually into a tidy silver-flecked carpet.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in light to full shade; this Japanese selection is a slow spreader well suited to woodland beds where it won't be crowded out.

directions: Roundabout bears medium green, rounded evergreen leaves about two inches across, dotted with small dollops of silver, forming a low, slowly spreading carpet. Small flesh-colored flowers open in late winter tucked within the leaf axils, close to the soil. It works equally well as a specimen in a shaded container or massed as a weed-suppressing groundcover in a woodland bed.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring as new growth begins, in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; cut the clump back to the ground in late winter before new shoots emerge.

directions: Mulled Wine is a Japanese forest grass selection discovered as a shoot mutation of 'Aureola' in a Dorset, UK garden, bred on by Knoll Gardens. It carries tri-color striped leaves in yellow, light green, and emerald through summer, then turns a warm burgundy-red in autumn, extending the season of interest beyond the typical gold-and-green display of other hakonechloa. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; like other forest grasses it is slow to establish but forms an increasingly handsome cascading mound over several seasons.
